claims.text: AlCoCrFeNi2.1 is an as-cast eutectic high-entropy alloy with a fine lamellar FCC/B2 microstructure.
The as-cast AlCoCrFeNi2.1 alloy has an interlamellar spacing of approximately 2 μm.
The alternating FCC and B2 lamellae respectively constitute soft and hard phases.
The as-cast alloy has a room-temperature fracture stress of approximately 944 MPa.
The as-cast alloy has a room-temperature tensile elongation of approximately 25%.
Approximately 5% cold deformation followed by a brief low-temperature anneal will refine the eutectic lamellar microstructure.
Approximately 5% cold deformation followed by a brief low-temperature anneal will increase both tensile strength and ductility relative to the as-cast state.
Slight cold work introduces dislocations into the eutectic alloy.
Slight cold work refines the alloy's lamellar structure.
The refined lamellar spacing and increased dislocation density create additional barriers to dislocation motion and thereby strengthen the alloy.
A controlled dislocation density in the alternating phases enhances strain hardening.
The proposed processing retains a continuous soft-phase network that helps preserve ductility.
A brief low-temperature anneal relieves local stress concentrations and recovers some ductility.
The low-temperature anneal can recover ductility without significant lamellar coarsening or phase transformation.
The processed alloy will exhibit an ultimate tensile strength improvement of approximately 20% or more over the as-cast state.
The processed alloy will maintain or modestly increase tensile ductility relative to the as-cast state.
The benefit should hold at room temperature under quasistatic loading near 1 × 10^-3 s^-1.
The benefit depends on keeping deformation near 5% and annealing sufficiently mild to avoid excessive coarsening or brittle-phase formation.
